name: Introduction to Automated Reasoning
description: Formal modeling and specification (for example, alloy); operational semantics via labeled transition systems and execution traces; concurrency modeling using process algebras; interactive and automated theorem proving (lean, Coq); program correctness via Hoare logic, loop invariants, and inductive proofs (KeY-Hoare); behavioral equivalence using bisimulation and coinduction; temporal logic (for example, LTL/CTL) for reasoning about safety, liveness, and fairness properties; symbolic execution (for example, KLEE, CBMC); static program analysis including data flow analysis and abstract interpretation; satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) solving over linear integer arithmetic (LIA), including the simplex algorithm (with tools such as Z3, Gurobi); tool-based labs and formal proof construction exercises.
